title: Finite cohomological dimension permits unbounded acyclic-complex computation
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], let $\mathcal B$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], and let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive and left exact, with right derived functors $R^qF$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Suppose there is an integer $d\geq0$ such that $R^qF(M)=0$ for every $M\in\mathcal A$ and every $q>d$. Use cochain complexes, quasi-isomorphisms and derived categories as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then the unbounded right derived functor $RF:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ exists, with its natural comparison $\alpha_L:Q_{\mathcal B}(F(L^\bullet))\to RF(Q_{\mathcal A}L^\bullet)$. For every unbounded complex $L^\bullet$ whose terms are $F$-acyclic [def-sp-acyclic], meaning $R^qF(L^r)=0$ for all $r\in\mathbf Z$ and $q>0$, $\alpha_L$ is an isomorphism. In particular, these isomorphisms identify the derived images of maps of such complexes with the termwise images under $F$, by naturality of $\alpha$.

proof.text: Let RF be the existing unbounded right-derived functor of F. Define α on a complex K as the composite of the inverse quotient comparison for B, the image under Qh of the inverse homotopy-category factorization of F, the canonical right-derived unit at the homotopy quotient of K, and RF applied to the quotient comparison for A. Naturality follows from naturality of the unit and of the factorization isomorphism, together with functoriality of Qh and RF.

source.place: existing right-derived functor and unit API; target module definition of α

proof.text: For any derived functor G and transformation β from termwise F followed by Q to Q followed by G, transport β across the quotient comparison isomorphisms and lift it through the homotopy quotient with Quotient.natTransLift. The right-derived universal property supplies a unique transformation RF ⟶ G. Uniqueness is checked after the right-derived unit using rightDerived_ext; existence is checked by rightDerived_fac and the lift equation, with cancellation of the quotient isomorphisms.

For every complex L whose terms are F-right-acyclic, the component α.app L is invertible by the finite-cohomological-dimension comparison theorem isIso_rightDerivedFunctorUnit_app_of_rightAcyclic, after unfolding the definition of α and inferring the surrounding isomorphism instances.

For complexes L and M with right-acyclic terms and any chain map f, the required square is exactly the naturality equation α.naturality f, after the definitions of the composite functors are unfolded.

lean.statement: theorem exists_rightDerived_computes_acyclic_of_finite_dimension {A : Type u₁} {B : Type u₂} [Category.{v₁} A] [Category.{v₂} B] [Abelian A] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{v₁} A] [Abelian B] [HasDerivedCategory.{w₁} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w₂} B] (F : A ⥤ B) [F.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F] (d : ℕ) (hd : ∀ (M : A) (q : ℕ), d < q → IsZero ((F.rightDerived q).obj M)) : ∃ (RF : DerivedCategory A ⥤ DerivedCategory B) (α : F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ RF), (∀ G : DerivedCategory A ⥤ DerivedCategory B, Function.Bijective (fun β : RF ⟶ G ↦ α ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft DerivedCategory.Q β)) ∧ (∀ L : CochainComplex A ℤ, (∀ r : ℤ, F.rightAcyclic (L.X r)) → IsIso (α.app L)) ∧ (∀ (L M : CochainComplex A ℤ), (∀ r : ℤ, F.rightAcyclic (L.X r)) → (∀ r : ℤ, F.rightAcyclic (M.X r)) → ∀ f : L ⟶ M, DerivedCategory.Q.map ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).map f) ≫ α.app M = α.app L ≫ RF.map (DerivedCategory.Q.map f))
